_tensor_spec_note: tensor_spec is the input-plane spec each checkpoint was TRAINED under, not the current one. v1 normalizes the distance planes by board_size**2, v2 by 2*board_size - a board_size/2 rescale of channels 8/9 (2.5x at 5x5, 4.5x at 9x9). Loading a model without passing its own spec silently feeds it planes on a scale it never saw. Every 5x5 checkpoint and the v4/v5 9x9 pair predate the v2 switch; the v9/v10 entries are spec 2. Runs record spec_version in the run dir's config.json.

2p_vector.notes: Trained with max^n MCTS (= negamax at N=2), 30 iterations, augmentation + gamma=0.99. 40/40 vs the greedy racer at 200 sims (20 games/seat, tensor spec v1) and plays the seat asymmetry optimally: seat 1 wins in 3 turns with ZERO walls (a pure race - two racers meet head-on and the second jumps the first, gaining a tempo), seat 0 wins in 4 turns with exactly 1 wall, the minimum investment that beats the deficit. Strongest model in the repo. Its gamma=0.97 sibling (runs/n2_5x5_g097_v1) scores 20/40 - identical seat 1, but 0/20 in seat 0 where it over-walls (3/game): a steeper discount suppresses paying a tempo now to win later.

4p_ship.notes: Trained with max^n MCTS, 70 iterations, augmentation + γ=0.99. Peak checkpoint iter 68.

2p_legacy.notes: Original scalar architecture. Trained with negamax MCTS, v3.2 notebook, 40 iterations.

2p_9x9.eval_win_rate: 97.5% vs the greedy racer at K=16 (80 games, seat 0 40/40, seat 1 38/40) and 8.3% vs depth-2 minimax - the strongest 9x9 N=2 result on the held-out protocol
2p_9x9.notes: THE N=2 DELIVERABLE (as of the 2026-08-12 held-out rescore). Full-size 9x9, 10 walls/player. max^n MCTS, 600 sims, gamma=0.99. Scores 97.5% vs greedy and 8.3% vs depth-2 minimax, where the greedy control itself scores 2.5% - the only 9x9 N=2 checkpoint that beats the racer at the minimax bar. It also races rather than walls: opening wall mass 0.26, against 0.88 for v9 and 0.84 for v10. TWO CAVEATS. (1) The lead over n2_9x9_v9 (91.2%) is NOT statistically significant: z=1.72, p~0.09 on 80 games each. Treat them as indistinguishable on the racer and separated only by the minimax column. (2) It is K-dependent in a way its training does not explain: trained at K=0, it scores 70.0% vs greedy at K=0 and 97.5-100% at K=16, so it must be served at K=16 (see _wall_candidates_note). ship.pt and best.pt are byte-identical here (same sha256; the run accepted 15 times, last at iter 145, and has no greedy_peak.pt, so the resolver shipped the gate champion). The path moved to ship.pt only to name the file that was actually rescored - it is the same weights this entry always pointed at. Which is the point: the earlier 'NOT DEMO-READY, 0% vs a greedy pawn-rush' verdict describes THESE weights. It came from training-time evals run at K=0, where the same checkpoint reads 50% at iteration 150; restricting wall expansion to K=16 takes it to 97.5%. The deficit was in the search, not the network.

4p_9x9.eval_win_rate: ~88-96% vs random (fair share 25%) BUT 0% vs a greedy pawn-rush
4p_9x9.notes: Full-size 9x9, 5 walls/player. max^n MCTS, 600 sims, γ=0.99. best.pt = accept-gated peak of n4_9x9_v5. NOT DEMO-READY: 0/40 vs the greedy racer on all 14 training evals. Same pathology as 2p_9x9. The vs-random number is saturated - do not quote it alone.

2p_9x9_v9.eval_win_rate: 91.2% vs the greedy racer on the held-out protocol (80 games, seat 0 39/40, seat 1 34/40) and 0.0% vs depth-2 minimax; 93.8% pooled at training time (iter 12, 600 sims)
2p_9x9_v9.notes: The best warm-started N=2 model, and the scientific result of the v9 generation - but no longer the served checkpoint. The 2026-08-12 held-out rescore put n2_9x9_v4/ship.pt at 97.5% vs the racer against this model's 91.2%, and 8.3% vs depth-2 minimax against this model's 0.0%, so the demo serves 2p_9x9. The racer gap is not significant (z=1.72); the minimax column is what decided it. Keep citing this run for what it demonstrates: warm-starting produced the first 9x9 model with BOTH seats over 90%, in twelve iterations rather than ninety-five. Full-size 9x9, 10 walls/player, warm-started from runs/pretrain_n2_9x9. First 9x9 model that both races and walls, and the first with BOTH seats over 90%. Identical to that run's ship.pt. Pinned to greedy_peak.pt by path on purpose: the run never accepted in 60 iterations, so best.pt is the untrained initialization, and pooled rate decays to 82% by iter 60. n2_9x9_v10 peaked lower (87.5%, iter 16) and does not replace this.

4p_9x9_v9.eval_win_rate: 40% best-seat (seat 0, 8/20) at the iter-12 peak; pooled ceiling is 25%
4p_9x9_v9.notes: Superseded by 4p_9x9_v10; kept as the record. Peaked at seat 0 8/20 (10% pooled) at iter 12, then the gate ACCEPTED at iters 20/24/28 while the per-seat rate fell to 0%, so best.pt and ship.pt both hold the dead iter-28 model. This run is why the demo pins greedy_peak.pt rather than trusting the accept gate.

4p_9x9_v10.eval_win_rate: 12.5% pooled vs the greedy racer (iter 8, 80 games); seat 0 10/20 = 50%, seats 1-3 0/20
4p_9x9_v10.notes: Superseded by 4p_9x9_v12 (repinned 2026-08-25); kept as the record. Full-size 9x9, 5 walls/player, warm-started from runs/pretrain_n4_9x9. Best N=4 result to date - seat 0 at 50% is 6x anything the six pre-warm-start runs managed (none passed 2/80). Pooled 12.5% is below the 25% fair share because only seat 0 ever wins. Identical to that run's ship.pt. Pinned by path: the gate accepted at iter 20, where the racer scores 0/80, so best.pt holds a dead model.

4p_9x9_v12.eval_win_rate: 15.0% pooled vs the greedy racer at the held-out protocol (K=16, 200 sims, 40 games/seat); seat 0 24/40 = 60%, seats 1-3 0/40
4p_9x9_v12.notes: Superseded by 4p_9x9_v13 (repinned 2026-08-26); kept as the record. v12 = v11 + the clone seat-0 value defense (clone_seat0_value_weight 0.0): the first N=4 run that never eroded to zero - it dipped to 3/20 at iter 16 and RECOVERED to 15/20. Repinned 2026-08-25 on the matched 40/seat ladder: pretrain 34/40 > v12 24/40 > v10 14/40, each step significant (v12>v10 z~2.2 p~.03 on seat 0). Still below the supervised warm start it was trained from (RL retains, does not yet add); only RL-trained checkpoints ship. greedy_peak.pt = iteration 8; identical to that run's ship.pt. Serve at K=16 (wall_candidates on the variant).

4p_9x9_v13.architecture: QuoridorModelMP (vector value head, N=4, factored policy head)
4p_9x9_v13.eval_win_rate: 20.6% pooled vs the greedy racer at the held-out protocol (K=16, 200 sims, 40 games/seat); seat 0 33/40 = 82.5%, seats 1-3 0/40
4p_9x9_v13.notes: THE N=4 DELIVERABLE. v13 = v12 + the factored policy head (move-vs-wall gate): statistically ties the supervised prior (82.5% vs 85% seat 0, z~0.3) and beats every RL predecessor (v13>v12 z~2.0 p~.04; ladder pretrain 34/40 ~ v13 33/40 > v12 55/85 > v10 37/85). In-run iteration 4 was a PERFECT eval: seat 0 20/20, pooled 25.0% = the racer ceiling. Lowest RL wall mass ever (0.078). greedy_peak.pt = iteration 4. REQUIRES the factored-head loaders from PR #69 - do not deploy this pin before that merges. Serve at K=16 (wall_candidates on the variant).

variants._note: Which registry model backs each (board_size, num_players) demo, plus the env settings it was trained under. max_walls matters as much as the weights: the walls-remaining plane is scaled by it, so serving a checkpoint at the wrong wall count feeds it planes it never saw. Read via src/utils/model_registry.py.
variants._wall_candidates_note: The MCTS wall-expansion budget K to SERVE this checkpoint at - the K it scores highest under, which is a measured fact per checkpoint and not always the K it trained under. Serving the wrong K fails silently: the model just plays badly. Two examples of the size of it: n2_9x9_v7 (trained K=16) scores 80.0% at K=16 and 47.5% at K=0, and n2_9x9_v4 (trained K=0) scores 97.5-100% at K=16 and 70.0% at K=0 - so restricting wall expansion helps a checkpoint that never saw the restriction, and the earlier rule of thumb 'serve at the trained K' does not survive that case. 0 means unrestricted, which is where both 5x5 checkpoints score best. Separately, and still true: a result SCORED at one K is not comparable to one scored at another, so never put pre- and post-restriction numbers in one table without a K column. See docs/restricted_wall_search.md and outputs/final/.
variants._max_turns_note: PLIES, not rounds - QuoridorEnvMP increments turn_count once per step, the same unit as max_game_moves in training and max_moves in the evaluator. Each value is the horizon its own run used (runs/<run>/config.json): 150 for both 5x5 runs, 160 at 9x9 N=2 and 320 at 9x9 N=4, set per variant to give every player the same ~80-ply budget. Serving N=4 at a shorter horizon than 320 scores as a timeout the games the measured configuration had room to convert.
